newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs trade mostly $0.50 lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs trade mostly $0.50 lower.

text.p: Cash hogs traded mostly $0.50 per cwt lower in U.S. Midwest direct markets on Tuesday, as livestock dealers said hog supplies were adequate to meet the needs of reduced slaughter schedules.

Interior Iowa sources said hogs traded $0.50 lower at $57.50 delivered to packing plants and $55.50 at country points. Illinois sources reported $0.50 lower trades of $58.00 delivered to plants versus an extreme top Monday of $58.50. Hogs traded at $56.00 to $57.50 at country points.
Indiana hogs traded steady to $0.50 lower at $58.00 delivered to plants and $56.00 at country points.
Ohio sources expected steady to $0.50 higher prices because of light marketings there but trading had not started early Tuesday.
Warm, dry weather in Ohio had farmers concentrating on replanting washed out corn fields and planting soybeans instead of marketing hogs, dealers said.
Cash pork prices were slightly higher on Monday, but several dealers said gains were not enough to encourage packers to bid higher for hogs.
USDA reported pork cutout values late Monday gained $0.11 to $0.03 per cwt.
